title: To Pimp a Butterfly
description: Kendrick Lamar’s third studio album was recorded across the United States with producers including Sounwave and Terrace Martin. Its hip-hop draws on jazz, funk, and soul.

title: OK Computer
description: Radiohead recorded their third album with Nigel Godrich, mainly at their Oxfordshire rehearsal space and a historic Bath mansion. The sessions took the band away from the guitar sound of The Bends.

title: In Rainbows
description: Radiohead first put out their seventh album as a pay-what-you-want download in October 2007. XL Recordings followed with a retail release later that year.

title: Wish You Were Here
description: Pink Floyd’s ninth album grew out of material developed on tour and was recorded at Abbey Road Studios. It became the band’s first release for Columbia in the United States.

title: In the Court of the Crimson King
description: King Crimson’s debut brought jazz, classical and symphonic ideas into rock. Island Records released it in 1969, and its approach helped define progressive rock.

title: good kid, m.A.A.d city
description: Kendrick Lamar’s second studio album features Drake, Dr. Dre, Jay Rock and Anna Wise. The record follows a young Lamar through episodes of his life in Compton.

title: Kid A
description: On their fourth album, Radiohead and producer Nigel Godrich worked in several European studios. The band moved toward electronic music, jazz and krautrock.

title: Madvillainy
description: Madvillainy is the sole studio album by Madvillain, the duo of rapper MF DOOM and producer Madlib. Stones Throw released it in March 2004.

title: The Dark Side of the Moon
description: Pink Floyd developed their eighth studio album during live performances. The resulting concept record follows pressures and experiences that shape everyday life.

title: Loveless
description: Kevin Shields led sessions for My Bloody Valentine’s second album from 1989 to 1991, layering guitars and experimenting with their sound. Creation released it in the UK and Sire in the US.

title: Abbey Road
description: Abbey Road was the eleventh Beatles studio album and the last one they recorded together. Apple Records released it in September 1969, ahead of the delayed Let It Be.

title: Remain in Light
description: Talking Heads recorded their fourth album in the Bahamas and New York in summer 1980. It was their last album with Brian Eno as producer.

title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
description: David Bowie co-produced his fifth studio album with Ken Scott. It features the Spiders from Mars backing band, including guitarist Mick Ronson.

title: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven
description: Godspeed You! Black Emperor’s second studio album first appeared as a double LP on Constellation. It consists of four long pieces, each divided into movements.

title: Illmatic
description: Nas recorded his debut at several New York studios in 1992 and 1993. Columbia released it in 1994, with production by DJ Premier, Large Professor, Pete Rock and others.

title: Revolver
description: The Beatles made fuller use of studio recording techniques on their seventh album. Revolver arrived with the double A-side single “Eleanor Rigby” and “Yellow Submarine” in August 1966.

title: Vespertine
description: For her fourth studio album, Björk made intricate electronic music with a deliberately quiet, domestic feel. It first appeared in Japan in August 2001.

title: Paranoid
description: Black Sabbath’s second album came out first in the UK on Vertigo in September 1970. It includes “War Pigs,” “Iron Man” and the title track.

title: The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady
description: Charles Mingus recorded this extended composition in January 1963. Conceived in part as a ballet, the piece is divided into six movements spread across four tracks.

title: Disintegration
description: The Cure recorded their eighth studio album at Hookend in Oxfordshire with co-producer David M. Allen. Fiction Records released it in May 1989.

title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
description: The Velvet Underground and singer Nico recorded their debut during the era of Andy Warhol’s Exploding Plastic Inevitable shows. Warhol designed the banana sleeve.

title: A Love Supreme
description: John Coltrane recorded this suite in one December 1964 session with McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Garrison and Elvin Jones. The session took place at Van Gelder Studio in New Jersey.

title: Animals
description: Pink Floyd produced their tenth studio album at Britannia Row, their new London studio. Its longer pieces carry forward an approach the band had developed on earlier records.

title: Red
description: King Crimson produced and recorded their seventh studio album at Olympic Studios in London in summer 1974. Island issued it in the UK, with Atlantic handling North America and Japan.

title: Kind of Blue
description: Miles Davis recorded this sextet album for Columbia with John Coltrane, Cannonball Adderley, Bill Evans, Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb. Wynton Kelly plays piano on one track.

title: Songs in the Key of Life
description: Stevie Wonder’s eighteenth studio album arrived on Tamla as two LPs and a bonus EP. It brought the run of ambitious records he made in the early 1970s to its peak.

title: Long Season
description: Fishmans turned an earlier single into one 35-minute composition for their sixth studio album. Polydor first released the record in Japan in 1996.

title: Pet Sounds
description: Brian Wilson arranged and produced the Beach Boys’ eleventh studio album, writing much of it with Tony Asher. The sessions built on the orchestral sound of the group’s previous record.

title: IGOR
description: Tyler, the Creator produced the album himself. Released on Columbia in 2019, it includes contributions from Solange, Playboi Carti, Lil Uzi Vert and others.

title: Heaven or Las Vegas
description: Cocteau Twins made their sixth album at September Sound in Twickenham. It followed Blue Bell Knoll and was released by 4AD in 1990.

title: My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
description: Kanye West’s fifth album brought together producers including Mike Dean, No I.D., Jeff Bhasker and RZA. Def Jam and Roc-A-Fella released it in November 2010.

title: The College Dropout
description: Before releasing his debut, Kanye West had built a reputation producing records for artists including Jay-Z and Talib Kweli. The College Dropout arrived on Roc-A-Fella and Def Jam in 2004.

title: Dummy
description: Portishead made their studio debut on Go! Beat Records in 1994. Dummy helped bring trip-hop to a wider audience and won the 1995 Mercury Music Prize.

title: Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers)
description: Wu-Tang Clan recorded their debut mostly at Firehouse Studio in New York. Loud and RCA released it in 1993 under the title that introduced the group to a wide audience.

title: Spiderland
description: Slint made their second and final studio album with Brian McMahan, David Pajo, Todd Brashear and Britt Walford. Touch and Go released it in March 1991.

title: Pink Moon
description: Nick Drake’s third and final album was recorded with a sparer approach than his previous work. It was the only one of his studio albums released in North America during his lifetime.

title: In the Aeroplane Over the Sea
description: Neutral Milk Hotel’s final studio album combines indie rock and psychedelic folk with distorted textures and lo-fi recording. Merge released it in February 1998.

title: The Money Store
description: Death Grips followed the mixtape Exmilitary with their first studio album. Before its official April 2012 release, the trio sold cassette copies at Coachella.

title: Souvlaki
description: Slowdive recorded their second studio album in 1992. Released by Creation the next year, it became one of the group’s most enduring records.

title: The Queen Is Dead
description: Johnny Marr and Morrissey wrote much of the Smiths’ third album after the band returned to Greater Manchester. Rough Trade released it in June 1986.

title: The Glow Pt. 2
description: The Microphones recorded this third studio album on analog gear at Dub Narcotic in Olympia, Washington. K Records issued it in September 2001.

title: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
description: The Beatles’ eighth studio album put the recording studio, sleeve design, and an extended album concept at the center of the work. It arrived in Britain in May 1967.

title: What’s Going On
description: Marvin Gaye recorded his eleventh studio album at studios in Detroit and West Hollywood. Tamla, Motown’s subsidiary, released it in May 1971.

title: Discovery
description: On their second album, Daft Punk moved from the Chicago house influence of Homework toward disco, garage house and R&B. Virgin released it in 2001.

title: Homogenic
description: Björk’s third studio album pairs electronic beats with string textures. She produced it with collaborators including Mark Bell and Guy Sigsworth.

title: Blonde
description: Frank Ocean’s second studio album followed his visual album Endless by one day in August 2016. It first reached listeners through iTunes and Apple Music.

title: Unknown Pleasures
description: Joy Division recorded their debut with Martin Hannett at Strawberry Studios over three weekends in April 1979. Factory Records released it that June.

title: Either/Or
description: Elliott Smith recorded his third album in several locations, mainly in Portland, while he was still playing in Heatmiser. Smith, Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf produced it.

title: F♯ A♯ ∞
description: Godspeed You! Black Emperor first issued their debut on a single Constellation LP in 1997. A substantially different CD version followed on Kranky in 1998.

title: In a Silent Way
description: Miles Davis recorded the material for this album in one February 1969 session at CBS’s 30th Street Studio. Producer Teo Macero shaped the recordings into the released album.

title: Atrocity Exhibition
description: Paul White produced most of Danny Brown’s third studio album. The album features guests including Kendrick Lamar, Earl Sweatshirt, Kelela and B-Real.

title: The Low End Theory
description: Q-Tip led production on A Tribe Called Quest’s second studio album. Most recording took place at New York’s Battery Studios before Jive released it in September 1991.

title: The Beatles (White Album)
description: The Beatles’ only studio double album arrived in a plain white sleeve with the band’s name embossed. That stripped-back design followed the ornate presentation of Sgt. Pepper.

title: Selected Ambient Works 85–92
description: Richard D. James recorded the music for his first Aphex Twin album to cassette. The Belgian label Apollo released this collection of ambient techno in November 1992.

title: Close to the Edge
description: Yes’s fifth studio album contains three extended tracks with the title suite occupying one side. Atlantic released it in Britain and the United States in September 1972.

title: Hounds of Love
description: Kate Bush’s fifth studio album pairs a side of individual songs with the connected suite The Ninth Wave. EMI released it in September 1985.

title: Blackstar
description: David Bowie recorded his final studio album in New York with Tony Visconti and a group of jazz musicians. It was released on Bowie’s 69th birthday.

title: Deathconsciousness
description: Have a Nice Life released their debut through Enemies List Home Recordings in 2008. Dense layers and lo-fi production shape its mix of shoegaze and post-punk.

title: Nevermind
description: Butch Vig produced Nirvana’s second studio album. Recorded in California and Wisconsin, it brought a more polished sound to the band’s songs.

title: Mm..Food
description: MF DOOM built this album around food, turning culinary language into jokes, metaphors, and double meanings. Rhymesayers released it in November 2004.

title: Illinois
description: Sufjan Stevens’ fifth album tells stories tied to Illinois, from local landmarks to historical figures. It followed Michigan as his second album built around a US state.

title: Low
description: Low opens David Bowie’s Berlin Trilogy, made with Brian Eno and producer Tony Visconti. Short rock songs sit alongside longer instrumental pieces.

title: Marquee Moon
description: Television rehearsed these songs extensively before recording their Elektra debut. Its sound rests on the interplay between guitarists Tom Verlaine and Richard Lloyd.

title: Highway 61 Revisited
description: Dylan pushed further into electric music on his sixth album, recording with rock musicians as his backing band. The songs pair blues rhythms with his increasingly vivid writing.

title: Bitches Brew
description: Miles Davis recorded these sessions in New York in August 1969. The album expanded his experimentation with electric instruments into a double LP for Columbia.

title: Endtroducing.....
description: DJ Shadow assembled his debut almost entirely from vinyl samples. He spent two years editing and layering the sources on an Akai sampler.

title: Grace
description: Jeff Buckley recorded his only studio album with producer Andy Wallace. Its arrangements move between originals, standards, and reinterpretations of other songwriters’ work.

title: Master of Reality
description: Black Sabbath recorded their third album at Island Studios with longtime producer Rodger Bain. Its heavy, low-tuned sound influenced later stoner and sludge metal.

title: In Utero
description: For their final studio album, Nirvana brought in Steve Albini and pursued a rougher sound. DGC released it in September 1993.

title: Soundtracks for the Blind
description: Michael Gira built this Swans double album from recordings gathered across years. It combines band performances with archival tapes and other found sounds.

title: Donuts
description: Released on J Dilla’s 32nd birthday, Donuts packs 31 instrumental pieces into a continuous loop. It was his last album released during his lifetime.

title: Led Zeppelin IV
description: Led Zeppelin’s untitled fourth album was produced by Jimmy Page and recorded largely at Headley Grange. It includes “Black Dog” and “Stairway to Heaven.”

title: Ants From Up There
description: Black Country, New Road recorded their second album at Chale Abbey with live engineer Sergio Maschetzko. It was the last album with founding vocalist Isaac Wood.

title: Doolittle
description: Pixies’ second album became the band’s breakthrough after its 1989 release on 4AD. Its wiry arrangements shift quickly between melodic hooks and noisy guitar.

title: Late Registration
description: Kanye West recorded his second album over roughly a year, working with producer Jon Brion in Hollywood and New York. It broadens the sound of his debut with layered arrangements.

title: Electric Ladyland
description: Jimi Hendrix took sole production credit on this final Jimi Hendrix Experience studio album. The 1968 double LP was the group’s only US number-one album.

title: The Downward Spiral
description: Nine Inch Nails’ second studio album follows a character’s descent into self-destruction. The tracks move between industrial noise, electronic textures and quieter passages.

title: Mezzanine
description: Massive Attack turned toward a darker, more atmospheric sound on their third album, drawing from post-punk, industrial music, hip-hop and dub.

title: The Doors
description: The Doors recorded their debut at Sunset Sound with producer Paul A. Rothchild. It features the full-length “Light My Fire” and closes with “The End.”

title: Station to Station
description: Station to Station introduced Bowie’s Thin White Duke persona. He co-produced the album with Harry Maslin, recording most of it at Cherokee Studios in Los Angeles.

title: Ride the Lightning
description: Metallica recorded their second album in Copenhagen with Flemming Rasmussen. It arrived on the independent Megaforce label in July 1984.

title: Laughing Stock
description: Talk Talk’s final album was made after bassist Paul Webb left, with Mark Hollis and Lee Harris leading the sessions. The music makes room for silence, texture and improvisation.

title: Imaginal Disk
description: Magdalena Bay duo Mica Tenenbaum and Matthew Lewin wrote and produced this concept album themselves. Its story follows a character named True after she encounters a disc.

title: Blood on the Tracks
description: Dylan returned to Columbia for his fifteenth studio album. He began recording it in New York and revisited several tracks in Minnesota before it was released.

title: Blonde on Blonde
description: Dylan started recording this double album in New York with members of the Hawks among his backing musicians. Sessions later moved to Nashville and the record came out in 1966.

title: Symbolic
description: Death’s sixth album took a more melodic direction while retaining the band’s intricate playing. It was the only Death album to feature guitarist Bobby Koelble and bassist Kelly Conlon.

title: Karma
description: Pharoah Sanders released this spiritual jazz album through Impulse! in 1969. Its centerpiece is the extended “The Creator Has a Master Plan.”

title: Carrie & Lowell
description: Sufjan Stevens produced his seventh album for Asthmatic Kitty with contributions from Thomas Bartlett, Laura Veirs and other collaborators. It returns to a spare folk sound.

title: Closer
description: Martin Hannett produced Joy Division’s second and final studio album. Factory Records released it in July 1980, after singer Ian Curtis’s death.

title: Aquemini
description: Outkast’s third album takes its name from Big Boi’s and André 3000’s zodiac signs. Their differing personalities are a recurring theme throughout the record.
